And we will carry on until the day we bring that light to the surface.|"[[The Past]]"|sound=Betty Pearson.ogg}} '''Betty Pearson''' is a resident of [[Vault 33]] and a pre-[[Great War|War]] employee of the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] {{In|FOTV}}. She becomes the [[overseer]] of Vault 33 in [[Timeline#2296|2296]] after the abduction of [[Hank MacLean]]. ==Background== [[File:FOTV s1 ep8 Young Betty.png|thumb|250px|left|Betty meets [[Cooper Howard]]]] Betty was a [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] employee before the [[Great War]], working as an executive assistant in the corporation's [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Southern California headquarters]] and is from [[Solvang]], [[State#California|California]].{{FOTV|2|4}} She met [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] when he visited the building and admitted to him that some of the corporation's knowledge was above her pay grade. She requested that Cooper meet his wife [[Barb Howard|Barb]]'s executive assistant [[Hank MacLean|Henry "Hank" MacLean]], as he was a big fan of the actor's work. [[File:Betty's cryonic chamber.png|thumb|right|250px|left|Betty's cryonic chamber]] She was [[Cryonics|cryonically]] frozen in [[Vault 31]] on the eve of the Great War as part of senior junior vice president [[Bud Askins]]' management training program "[[Bud's Buds]]." She was unfrozen on February 15, 2246, and later sent to [[Vault 33]].{{FOTV|1|8}}, 21:00 During her time in the Vault, she eventually became overseer before later retiring at some point. Hank MacLean, also sent from Vault 31, took her place as overseer in 2271. Around 2283, Hank orchestrated the [[Fall of Shady Sands|destruction of Shady Sands]], seemingly killing his wife [[Rose MacLean|Rose]], who had previously escaped to [[Shady Sands]], in the process. Though Betty's involvement in this event is unclear, she was evidently aware of his actions, as she helped cover up the circumstances of Rose's absence, including lying to Rose's children about having helped bury Rose (though this may be true in a metaphorical sense). By 2296, Betty had joined Vault 33's three-person governing council, working alongside [[Woody Thomas]] and [[Reg McPhee]]. Due to Woody's and Reg's personality traits, and her own training and experience, Betty became the effective leader of the council. Later that year, Hank was abducted in the attack on the Vault by [[Vault 32 raider]]s, and a crisis soon erupted when the Vault's [[Water chip (TV series)|water chip]] broke. The governing council was disbanded, and Betty was elected overseer in Hank's absence, beating Reg and Woody. Around this time, Hank's son [[Norm MacLean|Norm]] grew suspicious about the circumstances of the attack and the secrets behind his family, the Vaults, and Betty -- which Betty also seemed to be aware of. Working with Askins, who was the overseer of Vault 31, she initiated plans to reassign a group of Vault 33 dwellers to settle the now-abandoned Vault 32, and later covered up Norm's disappearance from Vault 33 (as a result of his having infiltrated, and subsequently being imprisoned inside, Vault 31). Since then, Betty has been focused on solving the issue of Vault 33's broken water chip. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|A former [[Overseer]], Betty is part of Vault 33's governing council along with [[Woody Thomas]] and [[Reg McPhee]]. She cares deeply for the community and holds paramount its security and safety. Her no nonsense personality and natural leadership skills make her the real face of the council despite what Woody and Reg would like to believe.|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== [[File:FOTV S1 Amazon promo 16.jpg|thumb|250px|Betty approving Lucy's marriage application]] Betty approves Lucy's marriage application with [[Woody Thomas]] and [[Reg McPhee]]. During the wedding dance, Betty notices [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]] disappointed Lucy is married to [[Monty (TV series)|someone else]] and so she invites Chet to dance with her. [[File:Betty opposes opening Vault 33.png|thumb|250px|left|Betty opposes opening Vault 33]] Betty is mysteriously absent during [[Lee Moldaver]]'s raid on Vault 33, and it is unknown if she was hiding somewhere. When Lucy requests to open the Vault door to rescue her father, Betty feels everyone's first priority should be to maintain the security of the Vault and is against opening it. {{clear}} ====[[The Head]]==== [[File:The Head meeting Betty Reg Woody.png|thumb|250px|Betty, Reg and Woody leading the vault-wide meeting]] Betty appears during [[Norm MacLean]]'s job reassignment, saying that Norm put not just Vault 33 at risk, but Vault 31 and 32 as well. She claimed to have telegrammed with [[Bud Askins|the Overseer]] of Vault 31 and confirmed that they are unscathed. Eventually, she comes up with a new job for Norm: feeding the [[Vault 32 raider|raider prisoners]]. During the vault-wide meeting, Betty sits while Reg and Woody stand at the podium. When everyone discusses what should be done with the raiders, Betty feels Norm's idea of killing them should not be considered, although she empathizes with his anger. ====[[The Ghouls]]==== [[File:Betty brings pie.png|thumb|250px|left|Betty tells Norm to tread lightly]] Betty brings some pie she made herself to Norm. She comes to talk to him about how his vocalizing his desire to kill the raiders upset the Vault dwellers and that what he says carries weight because he is the only MacLean left in the Vault. Norm expresses how he feels guilty about hiding during the raid, and Betty notices how he feels angry about it. Betty comments that because Norm is clever, how he channels his anger can lead to dark places, and asks him to tread lightly before she leaves. ====[[The Past]]==== When Norm and Chet return from their morbid investigation of Vault 32, Betty asks the two men where they have been. They lie, but Betty seems suspicious of them. She is elected overseer of Vault 33 in 2296 to succeed Hank with 98% of the vote after his abduction, making her overseer again. During Betty's celebration ceremony, she is prepared to serve jello. Norm seems to disturb Betty when he prefers having a slice of cake instead of jello, which goes against the Vault Dwellers overwhelmingly preferring jello. Betty stares down Norm as he leaves, and his action suggests rebellion against her leadership. [[File:Betty and Norm.png|thumb|250px|Betty speaks to Norm in Vault 32 Overseer's office]] Later, Betty announces to the residents that she spoke with the overseer of Vault 31. The two of them agreed that the Vaults were too sacred to leave empty. She says the residents will partake in a resettling campaign. Norm asks Betty about his mother's Pip-Boy, and Betty replies that she buried it with Rose. ====[[The Radio]]==== [[File:Betty at Vault 32 door.png|thumb|250px|left|Betty tells the [[Vault 33 gatekeeper|gatekeeper]] to open the door]] Betty sends out new vault assignments to each dweller, with some staying in Vault 33, while others are to relocate to Vault 32. Later, Betty announces that [[Steph Harper]] is to be the new Overseer of Vault 32. Then she orders the inter-vault door to be opened and says good luck to the new dwellers of Vault 32 as they depart to enter. Meanwhile, Norm uses Betty's terminal to impersonate her and communicate with [[Bud Askins|the overseer]] of Vault 31, requesting a meeting. {{clear}} ===Season 2=== {{Quotation|After the raider attack on Vault 33 and Hank MacLean's abduction, Betty was elected to Overseer in Hank's place. With the Vault's water chip damaged, many in Vault 33 felt she was the obvious choice due to her previous tenure as Overseer.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ====[[The Innovator]]==== In [[Vault 33]], Betty Pearson discusses plans to repair the [[Water chip (TV series)|water chip]] with an [[Vault 33 engineer|engineer]]. [[Reg McPhee]] tries to help, but Betty hints that he should not interfere with important matters, suggesting, for example, that he create a support group. Reg takes her suggestion too seriously and organizes a support group for victims of inbreeding, which he himself is. ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== Betty is supervising a dwindling crop field when Reg crosses her while going on another water collection run for his support group. She chastises him for wasting water on his "snack club" that could be used to help the rest of the Vault. Reg is unfazed, reminding Betty she is dropping in popularity and had agreed to his terms for creating his support group, though he still meekly apologizes for his rude tone before hurrying away to get the water. ====[[The Other Player]]==== During another meeting of the [[Products of In-breeding Support Group]], Betty marches in with a team of [[Vault 33 guard|Vault security guards]] who deliver her orders to cut their snack budget and dissolve the group. Reg demands to see Betty, who walks in behind the lead guard. She calls Reg out for hiding away in his clubroom while she has been wanting to speak to him. Reg, realizing he might lose his place of importance, tries to make a popular stand by allowing the group to be dissolved but demanding the snack budget be left alone. Betty calls him out for celebrating during a water shortage in the Vault and exacerbating their problems by feeding people salty snacks. She remarks that they should not get special privileges just because of who their parents were, but Reg uses this statement to gain the crowd's support by claiming that they are still in "America" and they are all in the Vault because of who they are related to/descended from. Betty tries to calm the situation, but Reg takes it further, remarking on Betty's status as someone who came from [[Vault 31]] and acknowledging the Vault 31 dwellers' own claims that they are "plum different somehow." When Betty then tries to reference the Weevil Famine crisis, Reg rebukes her, saying nobody wants to hear about it anymore. This gains him the crowd's admiration, including a compliment from Marianne. As a final show of defiance, Reg grabs a handful of a jelly mold and devours it right in front of Betty, which fully turns the Vault 33 dwellers in the room to his side while Betty looks on in concern. ====[[The Handoff]]==== While loudspeakers in Vault 33 announce continued water restrictions, now prohibiting showers and even flushing the toilet, Betty sits in her office, lamenting that the situation is at a tipping point which leaves her with only one option. From a wall safe hidden behind a painting, she takes out Hank MacLean's Keepsake Box, which Steph demanded in exchange for giving water to Vault 33, while lamenting Hank's habit of keeping secrets. Later on, Betty stands in a shadowy corner of the inter-vault space as Steph comes to retrieve the box, where she then surprises Steph congratulates her on her engagement. Steph questions if this means Betty has spies in Vault 32, which Betty indirectly confirms. Betty pointedly notes that Steph still behaves like she did before the Great War, including her demeanor that often frightened her coworkers, then says that Betty herself has learned plenty in the time she has been awake. Steph draws a forced smile while responding that she had learned plenty of life lessons herself, even in the time before being frozen in Vault 31. As Steph goes to wheel the box out, Betty stops her and firmly reminds her fellow overseer that she gave her word to divert half of her Vault's water to 33. Steph matches her seriousness and says she will get what she wants, then walks back into her Vault. Betty calls out to say that she wants nothing to do with whatever Steph is planning, only wishing that it will not stop the Vaults from living in peace. Steph coldly responds that their deal was for the water exchange only, but she cannot speak for "[a] future [that's] bigger than [them]," leaving with a smile that unnerves Betty. ==Personality== [[File:Betty smiling.png|thumb|250px|Betty smiling]] Betty seems to be a kind and responsible member of her Vault; she also portrays herself as the coolheaded, experienced, moderator of Vault 33's governing council. She is seen comforting Chet, such as by asking him to dance during Lucy's wedding, as well as [[Norm MacLean]]. However, she is treated very suspiciously by Norm throughout the show, as if she is hiding a darker side. Norm finds it strange how Vault 32 was cleaned up, and Betty did not mention anything about what she found in it. While she claims killing the Vault 32 raiders is out of the question, it is unclear if she was the one who poisoned them. [[File:Betty sending assignments.png|thumb|left|250px|Betty sending out new vault assignments]] It is later revealed that Betty was one of Vault-Tec's employees who had been frozen through time. Betty claims she "buried" Rose MacLean when she died, although it is unclear if her choice of wording hints she was also responsible for nuking [[Shady Sands]] with Hank. It is also unknown if her motive for having people resettle into Vault 32 has a dark ulterior motive, especially given the water chip failure. However, she relocated Steph into the Vault as an overseer, another Vault-Tec employee; while this was done in continuation of the Three Vaults' experiment, Betty also notes that she hoped Steph would repay her by being cooperative in the future. She also made careful decisions about who was reassigned to Vault 32, including sending Chet while having Norm stay in Vault 33, suggesting she was trying to split up their partnership that was looking into the Vault's secrets. Later on, however, as the Vault's water crisis worsens, Betty demonstrates a greater deal of concern and dread about the fates of the Vault dwellers she oversees, including getting angry with and scolding [[Reg McPhee]] when his [[Products of In-breeding Support Group]] becomes a serious drain on their resources. She is initially angry with him when he refuses to obey her orders as overseer, but upon seeing that the Vault dwellers' support of her has fallen away, can only fall back on old platitudes that further harm her reputation in the Vault. After investigating Vault 31 and discovering Norm's escape and the death of Bud Askins, Betty fully reveals to Steph that for a long time before then, she had come to understand that Vault-Tec was never going to be their saving grace, and she wants to rededicate herself to ensuring the continued peace and prosperity of her Vault. This ultimately leads her to make what she sees as a [[wikipedia:Faustian pact|Faustian pact]] in having to fulfill Steph's demands to get access to 32's water and directly saying to Steph that she will not allow any of Steph's plans to endanger the safety of Vault 33. {{clear}} ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|Regular boys... can get angry and they'll just pee on the wall. When clever boys like you are angry... You're lucky not to have seen where that can lead.|sound=Betty clever boys.ogg|Betty to Norm in "[[The Ghouls]]"}} ==Appearances== Betty Pearson appears {{in|FOTV}}.
